content: This medication is intended for application to the distal rectum in patients who are unable to retain steroid enemas. However, its safety and efficacy have not been fully established. Potential side effects include burning, dryness, folliculitis, hypopigmentation, itching, pain, rectal bleeding, and secondary infections. Hypersensitivity reactions have been documented. It is contraindicated in cases of obstruction, abscess, perforation, peritonitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, and extensive fistulas or sinus tracts. Always follow the usage instructions provided on the product packaging. Sigmoidoscopy is recommended to assess the treatment's progress rather than relying solely on symptomatic improvement. Avoid burning or puncturing the container, and do not store it at temperatures exceeding 120°F. Since this product is not expelled from the body, systemic absorption of hydrocortisone may be higher compared to corticosteroid enemas. If there is no clinical or proctologic improvement within two to three weeks of starting therapy, or if the patient’s condition worsens, discontinue the medication. Rarely, anaphylactoid reactions have been reported in patients receiving corticosteroid therapy. In patients with latent tuberculosis or tuberculin reactivity, close monitoring is necessary as corticosteroids may reactivate the disease. For prolonged corticosteroid therapy, chemoprophylaxis should be administered. Live or live-attenuated vaccines are contraindicated in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids. Killed or inactivated vaccines may be administered, but their efficacy cannot be guaranteed. Immunization procedures can be undertaken in patients receiving corticosteroids as replacement therapy, such as for Addison’s disease. The lowest effective dose of corticosteroids should be used to manage the condition, and any reduction in dosage should be gradual. Complications from glucocorticoid treatment depend on the dose and duration of therapy, so a risk-benefit analysis must be conducted for each patient to determine the appropriate dose, duration, and whether daily or intermittent therapy is suitable. Kaposi’s sarcoma has been reported in patients receiving corticosteroids, particularly for chronic conditions, and discontinuation of the drug may lead to clinical improvement. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies on the use of corticosteroids in pregnant women. They should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Infants born to mothers who received corticosteroids during pregnancy should be monitored for signs of hypoadrenalism. Systemically administered corticosteroids can appear in human milk and may suppress growth, interfere with endogenous corticosteroid production, or cause other adverse effects. Caution is advised when administering corticosteroids to nursing women. This medication reduces inflammation by suppressing the migration of polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNs) and reversing increased capillary permeability. Its absorption is limited, with an onset of action typically occurring within 5 to 7 days. Hydrocortisone rectal cream or ointment is commonly marketed under brand names such as Anusol-HC, Proctocream-HC, and Proctosol-HC. To apply the product inside the anus, use the applicator tip, cap, or nozzle as directed by the product instructions or your doctor. Fill the applicator with medication as instructed and insert it approximately 5 centimeters into the anus. Apply the medication in and around the anal opening as directed. Do not use your finger to apply the medication inside the anus. Avoid covering the treated area with plastic or waterproof bandages unless directed by your doctor, as this may increase absorption through the skin. Wash your hands immediately after use and avoid contact with your eyes, nose, ears, or mouth. This product is typically used 2 to 4 times daily, or after each bowel movement, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results. Do not use more of this product, use it more frequently, or continue using it longer than prescribed. If you have been using this medication for an extended period or in high doses, do not stop using it suddenly without consulting your doctor, as some conditions may worsen when the drug is abruptly discontinued. Common side effects include redness, burning, or itching at the application site. Rarely, the medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, leading to systemic corticosteroid side effects, which are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for prolonged periods. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, seek emergency medical attention immediately. Before using this product, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to hydrocortisone or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Prolonged use of corticosteroid medications may impair your body’s ability to respond to physical stress. In children, long-term use may temporarily slow growth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary and not for extended periods or in large amounts. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses on this medication and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. Store this medication at room temperature and do not refrigerate it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
